messages:
Ana R: Heads-up — SAST job (sast-runner) flagged a HIGH: possible SQL injection in eng-runtime PR #482. Link: https://ci.redwood.dev/sast/1710901234 :eyes:
Ana R: @raj can you take a first pass? The pipeline attached a snippet but no stack trace.
devsec-bot: SAST report: rule 'SQL_INJECTION_PATTERN' matched. File: eng-runtime/src/db/query.go:142. Snippet:
```
query := fmt.Sprintf("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '%s'", userEmail)
rows, _ := db.Query(query)
```
Severity: HIGH, confidence: medium. Tickets: SEC-2319 created.
raj: Ack. grabbing the PR. Quick q: which ORM? looks like low-level db/sql usage. If it's using prepared statements elsewhere this might be a false positive.
Michael C: I pulled the PR. That file is a tiny compatibility shim; higher layers use sqlx.NamedQuery with param binding. The snippet in report is an old helper used only in tests.
Michael C: here's the real usage in prod code (safe):
```
const q = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?"
rows, err := db.Query(q, userEmail)
```
Jordan L: I can push a small change to replace fmt.Sprintf usage in the helper with parameterized queries and add a unit test.
Ana R: Thanks. Two things to confirm: 1) whether this helper is reachable from prod flow; 2) add audit note for the SAST triage.
raj: Running grep across repo: only present in eng-runtime/testutils/mockdb.go and legacy_v1_adapter.go (unused). So low risk but still want fix + explain.
Sophia I: Also, SAST flagged KMS usage in infra/secret-manager with broad principal: "compute-service-*". That's a real IAM misconfig. Who owns KMS policies? @sophia?
Sophia I: I own KMS for now. I'll scope the key policy to roles/secrets-admin and a service account compute/secrets-proxy only. Will propose minimal policy.
Ana R: Good. For the SAST false-positive path: please do 1) PR that fixes helper to be paramized OR mark file as test-only with comment, 2) link to exploitability analysis, 3) add a short note in SEC-2319 and request reviewer sign-off.
Jordan L: I'll open a PR in ~30m with both fix + unit test. Will add a comment referencing this thread and SEC-2319.
raj: For closure criteria, require: code uses parameterized queries OR file annotated test-only + owner ack, CI unit test added, and security reviewer approves.
devsec-bot: DAST scheduled nightly. Adding follow-up scan for change on merge.
Ana R: Also add an audit-log event when secrets fetch happens (secret-manager) so we have event for KMS decrypt calls. Suggest structured log key: audit.event=secrets.decrypt, include principal, key_id, request_id (no secret material).
Sophia I: Agreed. I'll add the audit hook in the secrets-proxy and wire to audit-ingest (retention 365d per enterprise policy).
Michael C: Small note: if secrets-proxy runs as compute service with broad RBAC, we'll tighten that to allow only secrets-proxy SA to call kms:Decrypt on that key.
Ana R: Let's also update RBAC doc: https://docs.redwood.dev/security/rbac#kms-keys to include the new policy and an explicit 'no broad principals' rule.
Jordan L: PR: https://github.com/redwood/eng-runtime/pull/491 created. Changes: replace fmt.Sprintf usage, + unit test, + SEC-2319 link in PR body.
raj: Reviewing now. Quick checklist in PR description would be useful: (1) exploitability, (2) tests, (3) audit/logging, (4) owners.
Ana R: I'll review the exploitability blurb. If all good, we mark SEC-2319 as 'resolved: mitigated' with note "false positive; helper test-only fixed" and keep the KMS IAM ticket open.
Sophia I: Opening infra ticket INF-765 to tighten KMS key policy and schedule rotation.
Ana R: Thanks everyone. Post-merge action items: 1) run full SAST + DAST on master, 2) verify audit events show up, 3) confirm RBAC policy applied. Tag me in results and I'll close SEC-2319. :thumbsup:
